script.text: Harder than flying to Pluto. Did Europe and Japan's Mercury probe just make it?

On Saturday evening, after eight years and nine planetary flybys, BepiColombo fired four thrusters for thirty-seven minutes, ESA says. The burn ran through its closest pass, about six hundred and thirty-five kilometres above Mercury, to slow the probe down.

It worked. ESA says flight dynamics confirmed the capture from tracking data. Reports put the first orbit at about five hundred and ninety by eleven thousand six hundred kilometres. Only NASA's Messenger has orbited Mercury before.

Why so hard? Falling toward the Sun, a probe speeds up. ESA says orbiting Mercury takes more energy than a trip to Pluto. Next, the two orbiters separate on December ninth and tenth, and science is planned from April twenty twenty-seven.
Will BepiColombo start its Mercury science on time in April? Yes or no?

upload.title: BepiColombo Is Now in Orbit Around Mercury #shorts
upload.description:
The European-Japanese probe BepiColombo has entered orbit around Mercury. ESA says the four thrusters of its Mercury Planetary Orbiter fired for 37 minutes on November 21, 2026, from 18:24 UTC, through closest approach about 635 km above the surface, and that flight dynamics confirmed the capture from tracking data. Reports give a first elliptical polar orbit of about 590 by 11,640 km. It is only the second spacecraft to orbit Mercury after NASA's Messenger (2011–2015). The two orbiters MPO and Mio are due to separate on December 9–10, with science planned from April 2027.

Sources: ESA (ESA Operations, BepiColombo arrival timeline and factsheet), Manila Times / Japan wire report, Starlust, AeroTime, Space.com, Tech Times.
